criteria.criterion: a test asserts a class without `fallback` builds an unwrapped model (no behaviour change)
a test asserts a class with `fallback` builds a FallbackModel whose default is the primary entry
a test asserts an error in the configured condition selects the fallback entry
a test asserts an error outside the condition PROPAGATES rather than failing over
the chosen `fallback_on` condition is documented in-code with the SDK-retry caveat
a test asserts a fallback entry carrying `endpoint` produces a model object built against THAT endpoint — not one silently built against the provider default

a test asserts every fallback client is registered on the SAME `ProviderSession` and is closed on teardown: with N Anthropic-typed fallbacks, `_closeables` holds N+1 clients and all are closed exactly once
a test asserts a chain containing a model with `supports_temperature: False` withdraws `temperature` for the WHOLE chain, not just when that model is the primary
a test asserts `provider_provenance` records the ordered `candidates` AND a `ran_model` equal to the model that actually answered — so a verdict produced by a fallback does not attest the primary
a test asserts `fallback_on` fires on a 429/529/5xx and on a transport error, and does NOT fire on 401/403 or on a 400 context-length error (the loud-failure cases)
a test asserts the `fallback_on` predicate is derived from `failure.py`'s `_RETRYABLE` frozenset plus `CHANGE_PROVIDER_OR_MODEL` — NOT a hand-maintained tuple of exception types

a test asserts the predicate returns True for `httpx.ConnectError` (RETRY_NOW — the down-local-endpoint case this ticket exists for), True for a 529/5xx, and False for 401/403 and for a 400 context-length error
a test asserts the 429 SPLIT: a plain rate-limit 429 falls back, a 429 carrying `insufficient_quota` does NOT (it classifies as INCREASE_PROVIDER_LIMITS)
a test asserts `capabilities_for` is NEVER called with a `FallbackModel` instance (it has no `.profile` and its `.provider` is None, so it would silently return default capabilities)
a test asserts `ran_model` is read from the returned `ModelResponse.model_name`, NOT from `FallbackModel.model_name` (which is the synthetic `fallback:a,b` string)

a test asserts the `FallbackModel` is used as an async context manager, so its sub-models' providers are entered and exited (pydantic-ai closes ITS clients; rebar-created retrying transports remain on `ProviderSession._closeables`, closed exactly once, never double-closed)
